- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.75) in recent days, reduce forecast overshoot by 10–15% to avoid overreacting to short-term momentum.  
- If sentiment is bearish (≤ -0.5) and price is trending down, avoid sharp downward revisions; instead, allow gradual mean reversion with slight upward bias to counteract panic-driven lows.  
- When model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >10% over 30d), check if sentiment was bullish recently — if so, apply a “mean reversion correction” by subtracting 5–10% from forecast tail.  
- If forecast spikes sharply after a recent dip (e.g., 3–5 days of low prices), reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to account for lagged market reaction.  
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.0–0.5), avoid extreme forecasts; use 3–5 day moving average of recent history as baseline for correction.  
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below 65% of historical mean, apply a “reversion bias” to bring forecast closer to long-term trend.
